subject: Math
subskill: Compare or Relate Mean and Median
prompt:
[Table 1]

The table shown gives the distribution of the years of teaching experience for the $20$ faculty members at a school. Which of the following gives the correct order of the mean, median, and mode of the years of teaching experience?
explanation: Choice A is correct. The mode is the value with the highest frequency, which is $12$. The median is the average of the $10$th and $11$th values when the data are listed in order from least to greatest. The cumulative frequencies are $6, 11, 15, 17, 18, 19, 20$, so the $10$th and $11$th values are both $13$, giving a median of $13$. The mean is $\frac{(12 \times 6) + (13 \times 5) + (14 \times 4) + (15 \times 2) + (16 \times 1) + (17 \times 1) + (24 \times 1)}{20} = \frac{280}{20} = 14$. Since the mode is $12$, the median is $13$, and the mean is $14$, mode $<$ median $<$ mean.
